speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed any abdominal distension or discoloration of your skin or eyes? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Electrolytes, Liver Function Tests, Lactate, Amylase/Lipase. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound, Erect X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: Within normal limits; Electrolytes: Within normal limits; Liver Function Tests: Within normal limits; Lactate: Within normal limits; Amylase/Lipase: Within normal limits. Abdominal Ultrasound: No significant findings. Erect X-Ray Abdomen: 'Double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "double bubble" sign on the X-ray combined with bilious vomiting is highly suggestive of duodenal atresia. Is there a history of polyhydramnios during pregnancy, and has the infant passed any meconium?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The classic "double bubble" sign on the erect X-ray, combined with bilious vomiting and a history of polyhydramnios (inferred from the need for early delivery and feeding intolerance), confirms this diagnosis. The family history of pyloric stenosis is a distractor; pyloric stenosis presents with non-bilious vomiting and typically appears weeks later, whereas duodenal atresia presents immediately with bilious vomiting.
